en: Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s monastery, together with a great saṅgha of twelve hundred and fifty monks.
There, the Blessed One addressed the monks:
"The formative forces of life are breaking apart; vitality is being cut short."
The wise fall away; therefore, exert firm vigor!
[1] Exert yourselves, you who have obtained the rare going-forth in the teaching of the Victor!
Those who seek liberation do not honor those who are deceived and deeply afflicted.
It is better for you to have given up your life, better to have fallen under the power of death,
than for you to have violated your moral conduct— so it has been praised by the Buddhas.
For one who gives up their life, only a single birth is lost;
but for one who violates their ethical discipline, ten million births are lost.
For one who gives up their life, there may be separation from kinsmen;
but for one who guards their virtue, there shall be meeting with the Buddhas.
Virtue is the supreme ornament; virtue is the perfume and unguent.
Virtuous conduct is a cause for joy; virtuous conduct is water that is cool.
Virtuous conduct alone brings tranquility; virtuous conduct is supreme in the world.
Wherever there are fierce poisons and serpents, one who possesses virtuous conduct is not harmed.
Through ethical discipline a monk shines; through ethical discipline one gains renown;
through ethical discipline one attains happiness; ethical discipline leads to the heavenly realms.
Just as for one deprived of eyes there is no perception of forms, so it is for one devoid of ethical discipline.
Thus, for one devoid of ethical discipline, there is no manifestation of truth.
Just as movement is not found for one who is devoid of feet, so too nirvāṇa is not found for one who is devoid of ethical discipline. [10]
Just as the auspicious vase is the essence and the source of all jewels,
so too is well-guarded ethical discipline the source of all dharmas.
Just as when the auspicious vase is broken, the fine jewels are lost, [so it is with discipline that is impaired].
Thus your morality is broken and the True Dharma is lost.
Having first destroyed your morality, you later desire nirvāṇa;
having cut off your ears, nose, and so forth in this world, what will a mirror do for you?
Much is heard with the ear, and much is seen with the eye;
those men who, having heard, practice accordingly, are destined for heaven.
For one does not obtain abundant learning merely through the faculty of hearing.
Those men who, having heard this, put it into practice, go to heaven.
[15] Whence can there be trust in women? Whence can one be dear in a royal court?
Whence can there be any essence in that which is like foam? Whence can there be permanence in enjoyments? [16]
There is no trust in women; there is no one truly dear in a royal court.
There is no essence in that which resembles foam, and there is no permanence in enjoyments.
As is a river, so is enjoyment; as is a boat, so is a household.
"As is a flower, so is form; life is like foam.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, and those monks, being uplifted in mind, rejoiced in his words.
The ninth discourse, titled "Endowed with Virtue," is complete.
